newsitem.title: UK: UK highly unlikely to join EMU in first wave - Blair.
newsitem.headline: UK highly unlikely to join EMU in first wave - Blair.

text.p: Opposition leader Tony Blair said on Thursday that it was "highly unlikely" that Britain would join a European single currency on January 1, 1999.

Speaking at a school in Redditch, central England, Blair said there were advantages in principle to a single currency but added: "It has got to be economically right for Britain and it should not be politically driven."
"It is a very big step and unless the economies fit together properly, it could do very real damage," said Blair, campaigning ahead of a May 1 election his Labour party is favourite to win.

He said Labour would take the decision in the country's economic interests but whatever that decision was, it would be dangerous for Britain to pull out of negotiations on the form the single currency would take.
"It is very important that we keep our place at the negotiating table," Blair said.
"I think it is highly unlikely we would be in the first wave but if we are, there would be a referendum on it."
